question: For $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, verify that $-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=(-\vec{a})+(-\vec{b})$.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluation of the left-hand side
First calculate
\(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
Therefore,
\(-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)
Step 2: Evaluation of the individual negatives
\(-\vec{a}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\)
and
\(-\vec{b}=4\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)
Step 3: Evaluation of the right-hand side
\((-\vec{a})+(-\vec{b})=2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)
Step 4: Comparison
Both sides give the same vector.
Final Answer
$-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=(-\vec{a})+(-\vec{b})=2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-\hat{k}$.

options.D: $-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and the stated relation is not satisfied.
